//: LubbDubb example config. Copy to lubbdubb.config.json (gitignored). Every key is OPTIONAL — omit any to take its default. The '//'-prefixed keys are inline docs; they are ignored at load, so this file stays copy-and-run. As shipped it drives the mock agent (agentMode 'raw' + fake integrations), so `npm start` works with no model or provider auth. Precedence: explicit overrides > env (PORT, LUBBDUBB_HOST, LUBBDUBB_DB, LUBBDUBB_REPO_ROOT) > this file > defaults. Four keys are DEEP-MERGED rather than replaced, so you can set one field of them alone: integrations, planning, validation, auth. Everything else — including issuePriorityLabels and ci.checks — is replaced wholesale. Full reference: docs/spec/02-configuration.md.
// heartbeatIntervalMs: How often (ms) the heartbeat fires a dispatch cycle. Default 300000 (5 min).
// maxConcurrentAgents: Hard cap on concurrently-running agents; seeds the live runtime control. Adjustable without restart via POST /api/control; a restart reverts to this value. Default 3.
// startPaused: Boot with dispatch paused (no new agents until resumed). The only config-level pause knob — live pause/resume is runtime-only and ephemeral. Default false.
// agentMode: How agents are launched. 'stream' = real Claude Code over headless stream-JSON (production default, runs unattended, supports the waiting/answer loop). 'pty' = real Claude Code as an interactive terminal (needs first-run onboarding done; this is the runtime that resumes across restarts). 'raw' = run claudeCommand/claudeArgs verbatim, prompt passed via LUBBDUBB_PROMPT (mock-agent demo + tests). Default 'stream'.
// claudeCommand: The agent binary to launch. Default 'claude'. Here it's 'bash' so the example can run the mock agent.
// claudeArgs: Extra args appended AFTER the harness's own, so an explicit flag here has the last word — which is why you must NOT pass --allowedTools here (it would silently drop the mcp__lubbdubb__* grants; use agentAllowedTools instead). A relative path naming an existing file is resolved to absolute at load (agents run in a worktree cwd). Default [].
// agentPermissionMode: Passed to `claude --permission-mode` so unattended tool calls don't hang. Default 'acceptEdits', which auto-accepts FILE EDITS ONLY — shell commands are covered by agentAllowedTools + the permission backstop below, so you should rarely need 'bypassPermissions' (which maps to --dangerously-skip-permissions and is refused by claude under root).
// agentAllowedTools: Tool allow rules handed to every agent as a `permissions.allow` fragment in --settings, in Claude Code rule syntax. These pre-approve the mechanical validate/commit/push commands an agent must run to take an issue through to an opened PR unattended. Anything NOT listed still hits the permission prompt, which the backstop (mcp.permissionEscalation) routes to you rather than hanging. Replaced wholesale. Default: the JS toolchain + git + gh, as shown.
// agentPromptDelayMs: Wait this long (ms) after spawn before delivering the task, giving an interactive REPL time to boot. Stream mode uses 0. Default 1200.
// agentSubmitDelayMs: PTY only. Gap (ms) between typing a message and sending its submitting carriage return — the claude TUI folds a burst into a paste and treats a glued-on CR as a literal newline, leaving the text unsubmitted. Set 0 to write both at once. Default 60.
// agentIdleWaitMs: PTY only. Safety net for a turn that ends without a sentinel: after this long (ms) with no terminal output at all, the session is parked as waiting so it reaches the inbox instead of sitting 'running' forever. Unlatched — output resuming un-parks it. 0 disables. Default 90000.
// agentWaitingPatterns: Extra literal substrings that mean 'the CLI is waiting for input' (backup escalation heuristic, PTY). Default [].
// agentResumeAttempts: How many times an agent whose process dies mid-run is re-attached to its own conversation before the harness settles it as failed. Counted on the agent row, so it survives a restart and bounds the agent's whole life, not one launch. 0 disables. Default 3.
// whitelistedApprovals: PTY waiting prompts the harness may auto-answer instead of escalating. Each rule: { match: <substring of the waiting prompt>, response: <text typed back> }. Default [].
// sessionTranscriptRoot: Where Claude Code keeps per-project session transcripts, which PTY mode tails for its legible transcript. Default '~/.claude/projects'. Override only if the agent runs with a different HOME than the server.
// promptTemplatesDir: Directory of operator overrides for the rule dispatcher's agent/escalation prompts. Each <prompt-id>.md replaces that prompt's built-in default; ids without a file keep theirs. A leading <!-- ... --> doc header is stripped before the prompt reaches the agent. A relative path resolves against repoRoot. Absent directory = all built-in defaults. Default '.lubbdubb/prompts'.
// docsFolderPrefix: Folder(s) the file-events hook treats as the artifacts area: any file an agent writes UNDER a prefix is promoted to an artifact chip regardless of extension, on top of the built-in report/doc heuristic (report extensions + any reports/ folder). Accepts a string or an array; a file promotes under ANY entry. A relative entry is worktree-relative; an ABSOLUTE entry (e.g. D:/docs) also matches files written under that real directory OUTSIDE the worktree and widens the artifact-serving boundary to include it. Unset = heuristic only.
// userId: WHO YOU ARE, to every provider the harness talks to — the one identity it acts on behalf of. Setting it turns on three gates together, because they are one intent (this harness works MY queue): (1) OWNERSHIP — '<labelPrefix>-watch' only counts if YOU added it, so nobody else can tag work onto the fleet; (2) ASSIGNMENT — tickets the harness FILES are assigned to you; (3) AUTHORSHIP — only pull requests you opened are surfaced, which is also what lets a merged branch of yours be reaped. One string rather than one per provider because one project is worked at a time and each project carries its own config file: it is a GitHub login where integrations selects 'github', an Azure UPN where it selects 'azure', and only one of those is ever in force. UNSET (the default) leaves all three gates off — any tagger counts, filed tickets go unassigned, every open PR is surfaced. That is the first-run posture, and it is why the 'fake' provider works with no identity at all.
// integrations: Which provider fulfils each capability — the swap switch. One provider per capability, deep-merged so you can override just one. Providers: 'fake' (editable, injectable world — the demo default), 'github' and 'azure' (real). Capabilities: sourceControl (pull requests), issues (issues / work items).
// github: Target for the real 'github' provider — required only when integrations.sourceControl or .issues is 'github' (ignored otherwise). owner/repo name the repository; filters.prAuthor narrows the PR slice to one author. All open issues are ingested (the watch/ignore gate decides what's acted on, not an ingest filter). defaultAssignee is the login that issues the harness FILES (a deferred finding, unrecorded work, a blueprint, a raised bug) are assigned to — not a filter, it narrows nothing; unset files them unassigned. Auth is NOT here — set the GITHUB_TOKEN env var so a secret never lands in a committed file.
// azureDevOps: Target for the real 'azure' provider (Azure DevOps Repos + Boards) — required only when integrations.sourceControl or .issues is 'azure' (ignored otherwise). organization/project/repository name the repo; filters.prAuthor narrows PRs by uniqueName/UPN, filters.workItemTag narrows work items to one tag, filters.workItemAssignedTo narrows work items to one assignee by uniqueName/UPN. When both workItemTag and workItemAssignedTo are set they AND (an item must match both). defaultAssignee is the UPN that work items the harness FILES are assigned to — it narrows nothing, and defaults to filters.workItemAssignedTo, since where that filter is set an item filed to anyone else is invisible to the harness that filed it. Auth is NOT here — set AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT (Basic), or leave it unset to use the logged-in `az` CLI (Bearer).

azureDevOps.// policyChecks: Which Azure BRANCH-POLICY kinds become CI checks, and how. Kinds: build, status, comments, workItems, reviewers, mergeStrategy, other. Modes: 'check' (an ordinary CiCheck — visible, routable by a ci.checks rule, dispatchable), 'advisory' (visible and structurally unable to dispatch or escalate), 'off' (not emitted). Unset kinds take the defaults: build + status are 'check', comments is 'advisory' (rule pr-review-comment already models threads at higher fidelity), everything else 'off'. An unknown kind or mode throws at load. Nothing here can reach the aggregate ciStatus, so widening it can never make a PR read as unable to merge. The example promotes work-item linking so an agent fixes it — paired with the ci.checks guidance below.

// labelPrefix: The prefix behind the cockpit's watch/ignore toggle, shared by PRs and issues. It derives two labels: '<prefix>-watch' ('work this') and '<prefix>-ignore' ('leave this alone'). The no-tag default differs by type: PRs are opt-out (watched unless <prefix>-ignore), issues are opt-in (ignored unless <prefix>-watch). Default 'lubbdubb', so 'lubbdubb-ignore' keeps its historical meaning as the PR exclusion tag. Set it to '' to disable both gates (PRs never excluded, all open issues acted on).
// issuePriorityLabels: Label -> priority weight for ordering issue pickup when headroom is limited (higher = first). REPLACED wholesale by an override, not merged, so you can define your own scheme (e.g. p0/p1/p2). Default { 'priority:high': 3, 'priority:medium': 2, 'priority:low': 1 }.
// issueDefaultPriority: Weight for an issue carrying no matching priority label. Default 2.
// issuePickupStates: Dispatcher-level, state-based pickup gate. When non-empty, only issues whose provider-native workflow state is listed are picked up (e.g. ['Ready','Doing'] for Azure). Meaningful only for providers with a richer state model than open/closed (Azure work items); GitHub issues are unaffected. Unset/empty = no state gate.
// issueInReviewState: The state a work item is moved to once a PR is open for it, so agents stop re-picking work already awaiting review/CI (e.g. 'In Review'). Takes effect only alongside issuePickupStates and needs a provider that can write state back (Azure). Unset = no automatic transition.
// planning: The planning funnel for multi-PR issues. ON by default. Every watched open issue first gets a PLANNING agent (rule issue-plan, on branch plan/issue/<n>) that reads the repo and submits a verdict through the plan_submit tool (or .lubbdubb/plan.json as the fallback): 'single' (one PR — falls through to normal pickup, unchanged) or 'parts' (a decomposition the part scheduler owns: rule plan-part puts one agent per part on issue/<n>/<slug>, stacked on its dependency's branch while that dependency's PR is open). Progress is mirrored to the tracker as ONE status comment per plan, edited in place; completion never closes the issue. A planner that crashes or writes no plan fails OPEN after the usual attempt cap: the issue routes to 'single' and is worked as it would be without plans, so a planner failure can never park an issue. OFF leaves the funnel out entirely — rule issue-pickup un-narrowed, no planner ever dispatched. Deep-merged.

planning.// maxConcurrentPartsPerIssue: How many parts of one plan may have agents at once — a cap rather than fanning the whole graph out as soon as dependencies are satisfied. These slots come out of maxConcurrentAgents, so one issue can occupy several of them. Default 2.
planning.// requireApproval: Put a 'parts' verdict to you before anything is scheduled from it — approve-before rather than replan-after. On, ingestion persists the decomposition as 'awaiting_approval', rule plan-approval proposes it once, and rule plan-part schedules nothing (its ready parts queue as 'unapproved' in Up next) until you accept. Rejecting retires the parts nothing was started for and works the issue as one PR. A 'single' verdict is never gated. Default true.
planning.// gitFetchIntervalMs: Floor on how often plan reconciliation runs `git fetch` before reading branch reality. The git observer is fetch-free by design, so without a fetch it never sees a branch pushed from another machine — and 'has the dependency actually pushed' is what a stacked part waits on. This only stops a deliberately fast heartbeat becoming a fetch storm. 0 = every pulse. Default 60000.

// COST NOTE: planning, the assay, the assessor and the retrospective are all UNCONDITIONAL — there is no switch for any of them. One issue can therefore spend an assayer, a planner, its part agents, an assessor and a writer. Only an 'unclear' assay verdict holds anything, and it ends the moment the ticket is edited or anyone comments on it.
// agentModels: Which model each KIND of work runs on, and how hard — keyed on the dispatch rule that proposed it. A rule points at a NAMED PROFILE, and a profile is a model plus an optional effort level and nothing else (claudeArgs stays the single global escape hatch, so a profile can never clobber the --allowedTools MCP grants). The name is the stable part: when a new model ships, one profile value changes and every rule pointing at it follows. Resolved ONCE at dispatch and stored on the task, so an agent resumed after a restart re-launches on what it started on and the run stays auditable — the cockpit's agent drawer shows it, and 'by task type' spend prices it. NEITHER value is validated here: only the installed claude knows which models exist and which of them take --effort, so a bad one fails at SPAWN as a failed agent, not at boot. What IS refused at boot: a profile written as a bare string, an unknown effort level, a byRule key that is not a pipeline rule id, and any name that resolves to no profile. The whole block is OPTIONAL and merges WHOLE rather than field by field — setting it replaces it, which is what lets you REMOVE an assignment rather than only add one. Omitted entirely, no launch carries either flag and the CLI's own defaults apply — which is NOT a neutral setting: the CLI defaults to the top of the effort ladder, so an unconfigured fleet is the expensive one. The values below are a worked shape, not a recommendation: substitute the models your CLI actually has.

agentModels.// profiles: Profile name to what it launches. 'model' is anything `claude --model` accepts: an alias (as below) tracks whatever is current for that tier, a full model id pins one exactly — pin when you want a stored run to say precisely what it cost on, since Task.model records the string as written. 'effort' is optional; omitted, the launch carries no --effort at all. The 'fast' profile below deliberately sets none, because the smallest models refuse the flag outright — so cheap-and-shallow is one lever OR the other, never both. 'rank' and 'description' are BOTH REQUIRED and are read by the harness rather than passed to the CLI. rank orders the profiles cheapest-first and must be unique: it is how the goal-profile gate says whether a proposal is cheaper or deeper than what is standing, and how the cockpit orders its dropdowns. description is the whole of what the ASSAYER is told about your profiles when it proposes one for an issue — write it as instructions to an agent about when to pick this profile, not as a note to yourself.

fast.description: Mechanical, well-specified work with an obvious shape: a one-line fix, a rename, a config change, a test that just needs writing.

standard.description: Ordinary feature and bug work — the change is contained, the approach is clear from the ticket, and no design decision is being made.

deep.description: Work whose shape is genuinely unclear, that spans several subsystems, that has to weigh a design trade-off, or where getting the approach wrong is expensive to undo.

agentModels.// default: The profile every rule with no byRule entry runs on, AND every dispatch composed outside a rule. Set it: leaving it unset is not 'the middle', it is every unassigned rule falling through to the CLI's own defaults, which is the top of the ladder. One line here moves the whole fleet.
agentModels.// byRule: The exceptions, by dispatch rule id. Only the rules that are genuinely cheaper than the default need an entry. Two things worth knowing before you extend this list: several rules SPEND NO AGENT AT ALL — work-item-in-review and work-item-back-to-pickup write a tracker state, pr-merge-ready merges, pr-ci-blocked/plan-approval/plan-blocked/issue-shortfall only ask a human, and pr-base-update's cheap arm is a provider-side merge — so assigning them a profile reads as a saving and buys nothing. And a rule whose verdict GATES something (issue-assay stops the funnel, issue-assess stops pickup) is a poor candidate for a smaller model even though its output is short; give it less effort instead.
agentModels.// PINS: byRule prices work by KIND, which has no answer for the one issue that is harder than the rule it arrived on. That is a TAG on the ticket, not a config key: '<labelPrefix>-model-<profile>' pins one goal's work to one profile, and it beats byRule for every dispatch on that issue except issue-retro (fixed to its byRule entry — a write-up gates nothing, so a deep pin there is money for a document no dispatch reads) and issue-assay (the stage that PROPOSES the pin, so it cannot run on it). Nothing needs configuring to turn this on; it is on wherever labelPrefix and profiles are both set. The assayer proposes a profile for every workable goal, and a proposal that differs from what is already standing HOLDS the funnel until you confirm it from the cockpit — one click, and an absent proposal holds nothing, so a crashed or capped assayer can never park an issue. A plan may also name a profile per part, which beats the goal's pin for that part alone. See docs/spec/02-configuration.md.

// closedPrWindowMs: How far back a provider looks for pull requests that have LEFT the open set, so a merged or abandoned PR is observed rather than inferred from its disappearance. Feeds the cockpit's 'Recently closed' list, the pr_merged/pr_closed world events, and plan reconciliation's ability to tell a merge from an abandonment. Costs one extra list request per snapshot per provider (no per-PR fan-out). Default 21600000 (6h); 0 disables the lookup, and every consumer falls back to the older 'absence means merged' reading.
// upNextOverrideTtlMs: How long an operator 'Up next' priority override survives after the harness stops tracking its origin. The override is refreshed every pulse its origin is still queued or staffed, so a long-running item keeps its priority; once the work is gone (merged, closed, abandoned) for this long the stale override is pruned. Default 604800000 (7d); 0 disables pruning entirely.
// ci: Per-check CI policy: what the harness does about WHICH check, in WHICH state. Rules are ordered and matched by glob against the check name (* = any run of characters, ? = exactly one, case-insensitive) — and against any alias the provider reports for it, which is how an Azure status policy is matchable by the label shown on the PR page as well as by its statusGenre/statusName key. The first rule matching on BOTH name and state wins. REPLACED wholesale by an override, not merged. Empty (the default) — and any FAILING check matching no rule — is the pre-policy behaviour: dispatch a code agent with the generic fix prompt. So this is purely a way to carve exceptions. onFailure: 'dispatch' (fix it), 'ignore' (somebody else's wall — the DEFAULT for a rule you write, since the usual reason to name a check is to stop acting on it), 'escalate' (worth a human's eye). 'states' says which check states the rule claims, default ['failing']; the only other value is 'pending', for a BLOCKING check that never fails but sits queued forever until somebody runs something (rule pr-ci-gate dispatches for it, on its own origin pr:<n>:ci-gate with its own attempt cap, and a gate an agent cannot clear escalates rather than looping). 'states' SCOPES the rule rather than extending it — a rule listing only 'pending' no longer claims that check when it goes red, and the red one falls through to a later rule or to the unmatched dispatch. 'guidance' is appended to the agent's prompt and 'urgent' sorts this PR's concern ahead of every other PR concern this cycle — loadConfig THROWS if either is attached to a rule that never dispatches, if 'states' is empty or names anything but failing/pending, or if a rule that watches no failing state is not dispatching (it could never fire). The verdict is per PR, not per check: one agent works the branch, all matched guidance is appended to its one prompt, and held checks are NAMED to it so it doesn't chase them. When nothing is actionable but something escalates, rule pr-ci-blocked asks you once. Nothing here can move ciStatus or merge-readiness — a waiting gate never makes a PR read as failing.

checks.guidance: Run the lint-fix skill; do not touch unrelated files.
These are flaky. Reproduce locally before editing test code.
Run `/pr-agent-review` on this branch. The gate clears when the review posts its status; nothing in the diff is broken.
Link the work item with `az repos pr work-item add --id <pr> --work-items <n>`. The work item number is the `<n>` in the branch name `issue/<n>`.

// repoRoot: The git repo the harness operates on; per-branch worktrees are cut from it. Defaults to the launch directory (process.cwd()), so the common case needs nothing. Set it (or the LUBBDUBB_REPO_ROOT env override) to point at a repo elsewhere; a relative path resolves against the launch dir.
// defaultBranch: The repository's integration branch. A NEW agent branch is cut from it (origin/<defaultBranch> preferred over the local ref), it is the base named in a PR's base-update prompt when the provider reports none, and a PR targeting anything else is treated as stacked. Existing branches/worktrees are reused untouched and never re-based. Not auto-detected — the harness may run against a clone whose HEAD is anywhere, and a wrong guess silently mis-bases work. Default 'main'.
// worktreeRoot: Root under which per-branch worktrees are created. A relative value resolves against repoRoot (not the launch dir). Default '.lubbdubb/worktrees'.
// deskRoot: Root under which desk (no-code) scratch dirs are created — one per task id. Relative resolves against repoRoot. Default '.lubbdubb/desk'.
// dbPath: SQLite file. Overridable via the LUBBDUBB_DB env var. ':memory:' is supported (tests). Default '.lubbdubb/lubbdubb.sqlite'.
// port: HTTP/WS port for the server + cockpit. Overridable via the PORT env var. Default 4300.
// host: Bind address. Default '127.0.0.1' — this machine only, because the cockpit can queue jobs and a job spawns an agent with write access to your repo. Set '0.0.0.0' to expose it on your network; doing that with auth.enabled false is REFUSED at startup. Overridable via LUBBDUBB_HOST.
// auth: Cockpit access control. 'enabled' (default true) requires a bearer token on every /api/* route and on /ws. There is deliberately no token key here — a secret must not live in a committable file: set LUBBDUBB_TOKEN, or let the harness mint one into 'tokenFile' (0600) and print it as the #t= link at startup. Deep-merged, so setting tokenFile alone does not silently disable it.
